content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart. I completed my butcher training in 2015 and have worked in a market meat stall and a family butcher shop, preparing meat and serving customers.

At Mesnica Kod Ante, I break down beef and pork, and bone, trim and portion meat for the counter. I also make fresh sausages and advise customers on cuts and cooking times. On a busy Saturday, I serve around 120 customers. This experience fits well with FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise of knowledgeable, honest advice.

Food safety is an important part of my work. I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate, rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily. At the Dolac meat hall, I cleaned and sanitised equipment and wrote a closing checklist following a hygiene inspection remark.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my butchery and customer service experience could contribute to your team. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a concise, professional, well-tailored cover letter. It clearly connects the candidate’s butcher training, meat preparation, customer service, sausage-making, HACCP knowledge, FIFO rotation, temperature recording, and cleaning experience to FreshCart’s requirements. The reference to FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise creates a credible company-specific connection. The examples are concrete, especially serving approximately 120 customers and recording temperatures twice daily. The letter could make the candidate’s full nine years of relevant experience and broader meat range more prominent, but it is already focused and persuasive.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-relevant terms including “butcher training,” “bone,” “trim,” “portion,” “fresh sausages,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “cold-room,” “temperature,” “cleaned,” and “sanitised.” Its simple headings-free prose and standard paragraph structure should parse reliably. Alignment could be improved slightly by using the job description’s exact wording “cut, portion and package fresh meat,” where truthful, and by explicitly mentioning lamb, since the candidate’s original information supports carcass breakdown of beef, pork and lamb. The associated CV supplies most of the structured keyword coverage, so the letter does not need to become substantially longer.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates the two must-have requirements: completed butcher training and more than two years of meat-counter experience, as well as HACCP knowledge. It also aligns well with the role’s core duties: cutting and portioning meat, advising customers, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, hygiene routines, and customer-facing counter work. The customer-service paragraph reflects FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable and honest advice. The candidate’s material shows a gap for the nice-to-have forklift licence; the candidate has only used a hand pallet jack. Other relevant experience—lamb preparation, paper wrapping, sausage production, apprentice training, and the 180-guest wedding order—is not necessary to prove eligibility but could add modest persuasive value if included selectively. The candidate has not worked in a supermarket or used tray-sealing/self-service labelling equipment, but these are experience gaps rather than defects in the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the opening paragraph, replace the second sentence with: “I completed my three-year butcher training in 2015 and bring nine years of experience across a market meat stall and a family butcher shop, cutting and portioning beef, pork and lamb and serving customers at the counter.” This makes the candidate’s total relevant experience and meat range immediately visible.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the paragraph beginning “At Mesnica Kod Ante,” change the first two sentences to: “At Mesnica Kod Ante, I cut, bone, trim and portion beef, pork and lamb for the service counter, and paper-wrap customer orders. I also make four varieties of fresh sausage and advise customers on cuts, quantities and cooking times.” This incorporates supported experience and more closely matches FreshCart’s wording without claiming experience with supermarket self-service packaging.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the food-safety paragraph, change “rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily” to “rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, keep the counter supplied, and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily.” Only retain “keep the counter supplied” if the candidate is comfortable that this accurately describes the documented counter routine; otherwise leave the existing sentence unchanged. This would mirror the advertisement’s stock-rotation and well-stocked-counter priorities without inventing a measured stocking percentage.

requirements.requirement: Completed butcher training or ≥ 2 years at a meat counter
requirements.quote: I completed my butcher training in 2015 and have worked in a market meat stall and a family butcher shop
I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate
